newsitem.title: USA: Central Parking to buy Square Industries.
newsitem.headline: Central Parking to buy Square Industries.

text.p: Central Parking Corp. said Monday it has a definitive agreement to buy Square Industries Inc., another operator of parking lots, for about $37.2 million.
Central will offer $31 for each of Square Industries's roughly 1.2 million common shares outstanding.

It will launch a tender offer of $28.50 a share in cash, and deposit $2.50 in escrow to be paid to either Square or Central shareholders, "based upon the resolution of two specific matters," Central said in a statement.
Of the escrowed funds, $1.99 per share concerns the execution of a lease at one property, and 51 cents relates to the resolution of certain tax issues.
Square Industries will become a wholly-owned subsidiary of Central Parking.
Square Industries' stock rose 25 cents to $28.50 early on Nasdaq. Central climbed $1.50 to $34.375 on the New York Stock Exchange.
The deal is subject to Central receiving at least two-thirds of the outstanding Square shares.
Square Industries, based in Jersey City, N.J., operates about 117 parking facilities, mainly in the Northeast, with $65.9 million in revenues in 1995.
Nashville, Tenn.-based Central Parking operates more than 1,360 parking facilities in 32 states, the District of Columbia, Britain, Mexico, Puerto Rico and Germany.
It had revenue of $143.3 million for the year ended Sept. 30, 1996.
